architecture.mechanism: Independent audited measurement — establishing verification protocols using standardized, independently verified measurement methods (analogous to the paper's Two-Meter Water Method) that replace reliance on assumptions and produce objective baselines for detecting degradation rather than depending on unverified reporting.
architecture.intervention: Install two independently metered and periodically audited sensor pairs on each chiller circuit — one measuring condenser water delta-T across condenser tubes (inlet vs. outlet) and another measuring actual refrigerant-side heat rejection throughput — establishing a verified performance baseline during clean conditions so progressive fouling is detected via measured deviation from audited baseline rather than assumed normal operation, triggering targeted acid descaling (CIP) within permitted 48-hour windows before capacity drops further.
architecture.expected_effect: Early detection of fouling onset before the 11% capacity loss manifests, allowing scheduled cleaning interventions during limited shutdown windows; reduces energy penalty (currently 22% higher kW/ton) by maintaining condenser heat transfer near design delta-T; converts reactive troubleshooting into planned maintenance aligned with the 48-hour annual limit.
architecture.falsification_test: If the audit-based monitoring does not flag fouling ≥5 days before the plant reaches its current 11% capacity-drop threshold at peak load (as independently verified against direct thermodynamic measurement of kW/ton), the mechanism has failed.
